column1: # parse-error-drop-census-s399.tsv — every file whose EMITTED CL contains a
# `;; PARSE ERROR:` progn, i.e. a statement the compiler could not lower and
# replaced.  This is the #138 family, measured over the whole population for
# the first time (s399, task #343).
# SINCE s435 THESE DROPS ARE LOUD AT RUN TIME, not silent.  The flip (ruled
# docs/fable-answers-s433.md §A.1, Option B phase 2's last step) replaced the
# `nil` with a `p-die` carrying the file, line, source text and reason, so a
# program that REACHES a dropped statement now dies there — perl-shaped and
# trappable — instead of running on without it.  The `;; PARSE ERROR:` comment
# is unchanged and still the key every counter reads, so this census means
# exactly what it always did: the compiler's own list of what it cannot
# lower.  What changed is the PRICE of a row — it is now paid by the program
# that runs the file, which is the point: a row here is a gap someone will
# notice.  (The counted drop is still not the whole #138 family: a statement
# the compiler lowers WRONGLY is invisible to this file either way.)
# THE PRICE, MEASURED AT THE FLIP (s435): 55 rows across 4 perl-tests files.
# The unit of the DECISION is the STATEMENT; the unit of the LOSS is the
# enclosing TOP-LEVEL FORM -- and a file-level `my` compiles to one `let`
# around the whole remainder of the file, so ONE drop can cost every row
# after it (perl-tests/method.t: 1 drop, 39 unrun rows).  perl's own loss
# unit for an untrapped run-time die is the whole remaining PROGRAM, and
# both measurement runners' p-load-with-recovery (#467) already narrows
# that to the one form, so PCL post-flip loses LESS than perl would given
# the same program.  A file whose loss is out of proportion PROMOTES its
# drop's owner task -- it does not bend the flip (ruled s435).
# A SEVENTH POPULATION IS STILL NOT COUNTED IN THE ROWS BELOW, but it is no
# longer unmeasured: everything transpiled DURING a run -- a fresh_perl/
# runperl CHILD program (transpiled from a STRING, so it is never a .lisp
# file) and any module the running program loads.  Task #472's instrument
# shipped s438: the compiler appends `FILE<TAB>LINE<TAB>TEXT<TAB>REASON` to
# $PCL_DROP_LOG for every drop, sweep-perl-tests.pl sets it around the RUN
# (never around the file's own transpile) and reports a per-file
# `child-drops` count plus the DISTINCT sites.  It is REPORTED, NOT GATED --
# rows are blessed by hand after the first measured run, like every other
# population here.
# FIRST MEASUREMENT of that population (s438, full sweep, 108 files):
# **241 drops in 98 files -- but only TEN distinct SITES**, and the two
# numbers say different things.  98 of the 98 files reach the SAME two, in
# perl-tests/t/test.pl lines 179-180 (`open(my $f,'<',$out) ? <$f> // '' : ''`,
# task #479), which every file re-transpiles because the sweep runs with
# *pcl-skip-cache*; closure.t alone accounts for 38 of the 241 by loading
# test.pl nineteen times.  The other eight sites are one file each:
#   * SIX fresh_perl/runperl child PROGRAMS, and six is the whole population:
#     bop.t's `formline X000n^\0,\0^\0for\0,0..10` and split.t's
#     `split//.0>60for"0000000000000000"` (the two known from the s435 flip),
#     blocks.t's two `BEGIN(){1} ...` shapes, lex.t's `sub ub(){0} ub ub`
#     (runperl) and `flock _$`, magic.t's bare `]`.  All but the first two are
#     programs perl itself rejects -- the row asserts perl's error -- so a drop
#     there is close to the honest answer already.
#   * ONE RUN-TIME MODULE LOAD, and it is a real gap in a real module: the
#     system perl's Devel/Peek.pm:59 `$num |= (1<<index($D_flags,$_)) for
#     split //, $on;` (loaded by undef.t) -- PPI lexes `<<index` as a HEREDOC,
#     task #483.
# So the seventh population is SMALL and its rows are OWNED (#479, #483); what
# it is not is unmeasured, which is what it was until s438.
# WHAT IS DELIBERATELY OUTSIDE THE POPULATION LIST BELOW, and its measured
# size -- so a hole is a number here, never an inference:
#   * t/japh/ -- 1 file (abigail.t), 2 drops.  RULED PERMANENTLY OUTSIDE
#     (s437): the companion population IS run-perl-suite.pl's @DEFAULT_DIRS,
#     where `japh` is excluded as obfuscated, so nothing runs those files and
#     they are not a measurement population.  Its two drops are the same
#     `1 while -f ++$file` shape as the rest of family 1.
#   * cpan-tests/modules/**/xt/**.t and **/examples/**.t -- 1 file
#     (Test-Simple's examples/tools.t), 9 drops, measured s438.  Author and
#     release tests, not the dist's suite; nothing here runs them.  All 9 are
#     the Test2 block-form family (task #478), same as the population's own.
# (The `.t` half of cpan-tests IS a population now -- see `cpan-t` below.
# The s436 A/B that found it reported 43 files / 92 drops over ALL `.t` under
# cpan-tests/modules; that is exactly these 42 rows plus examples/tools.t,
# and the split was re-measured on an f702da3 worktree, where the same 42
# files carry the same 83 drops -- nothing moved, the population is narrower.)
# Columns: <rel-path><TAB><drops in the file><TAB><the compiler's own message(s),
# with a count each>.
# Population (SIX, since s438 / task #473; five since s434 / task #462):
# perl-tests/*.t (111) + perl's t/ default dirs (527, op/cond.t excluded as
# always) + lib/**.pm (22) + cpan-tests/modules/**.pm (94) +
# cpan-tests/modules/**/t/**/*.t (289) + the 14-dist CPAN board's own
# Every `.pm` is transpiled with `--module` — the emission the runtime caches,
# and therefore the one that runs.  Every `.t` is transpiled as a PROGRAM,
# which is what it is.  The dist `.t` files are transpiled WITHOUT the dist's
# own lib/ and t/lib on @INC, unlike tools/run-dist-t.pl, because it was
# MEASURED not to matter: the same 42 files carry the same 83 drops either way
# (the one difference was the absolute path inside one message, which the tool
# now normalises).  The board lives OUTSIDE the checkout (~/.cpan/build), so
# its rows are refreshed only by a run that passes `--board`; a run without the
# flag leaves them alone and says so.  Measured with tools/drop-census.pl at
# commit d0b52e9 + this session's tools; 1m36s at 8 jobs for all six.
# TOTAL after the edits below: 19 files, 62 drops (recounted from the rows,
# s468bc; 18 in-repo files / 60 drops as tools/drop-census.pl reports them,
# plus the one board row, which a run without --board does not re-measure).
# The previous line said 17 / 57 (s461ar), 18 / 58 (s458al) before that, and
# 19 / 63 before that (s457aj).
# The two rows that LEFT in s457aj are t/io/open.t and t/op/utf8cache.t, both
# by EDIT with their cause: they were the SAME mechanism (#850) — a paren-less
# list operator's argument list may end in a COMMA, and the operator that
# follows applies to the CALL, not to an argument (`substr $x,0,1, = "\x{100}"`
# `(ok f(),'d',) || _diag $!` — both probed 5.40.3).  PCL swallowed the
# operator into the run, so the comma split handed `parse` an operand-less
# operator and the reducer spliced the run to nothing: "Fell through.  Missing
# case: []", which is what BOTH rows' messages were.  Fixed in the one ceiling
# (`Pl::PExpr::_listop_arg_ceiling`).  Suite effect, spliced into
# baselines/perl-suite-run.tsv: io/open.t 142/23 -> 153/35 (the file reaches
# its end for the first time), op/utf8cache.t 14/0 -> 16/0 FULLY PASSING.
# The previous line said 21 / 65 (s456ag), and before that 27 / 77 (s454ae; the pre-session recount there was
# 34 / 90 -- the s448o "34 / 88" line had
# gone stale when s451 edited the Mojo _Collection.pm count 2 -> 4; the ROWS
# are the authority and the sum is what the runner compares against).  The s440-era split was 4
# perl-tests files (5
# drops), 20 companion files (70), 6 cpan-tests modules (7), 42 cpan-tests
# dist test files (83), 1 board module (2), ZERO in lib/.  (s440 merge of agents
# A (#463 items 1+2: -3 companion files / -7 drops) and B (#466, #464: -4 cpan
# modules / -11 drops, -1 board): the two edit sets are disjoint; recounted
# from the rows at the merge.)  (At the s399 measurement, over three populations:
# 72 files, 379 drops; the s415 edit below is the largest single change and
# more than halves both numbers.  A count that RISES is not automatically a
# regression: a file that used to die at transpile can start emitting CL, so
# its drops become countable for the first time -- see the s405 and s408 edits
# -- and a file this census never listed can turn out to have been carrying a
# drop all along (the two s415 (d) rows).  Every rise is argued in its own
# edit note; the runner still FAILS on any rise it has not been told about.)
# The total is the sum of the rows below — recomputed s408, which is how the
# stale "382" this line used to carry was found.
# EDITS since the s399 measurement (a drop leaves this file BY EDIT, like a
# fail-baseline row — never by re-blessing the whole census from a run):
#   s468bc TWO ROWS ADDED, FIVE drops (17/57 -> 19/62), and both are the legal
#         kind of rise (ruled s409): a file that used to die at transpile now
#         emits CL, so its drops become COUNTABLE for the first time.  Task
#         #1037 made a ruled refusal a STATEMENT-level event, and the two
#         files below are among the seventeen that went transpile-FAIL -> rc 0
#         because of it.  Neither drop is new CODE -- both statements were
#         always unlowerable; nothing could see them while the whole file
#         refused, which is the #138 family's oldest lesson.
#           t/class/inherit.t 1 -- PPI lexes the unit-class header
#             "class Testcase1C :isa(Testcase1B) 1.000;" as a Token::Label, so
#             the statement falls through the term walker.  Inside the class
#             feature, which PCL refuses; no separate owner.
#           t/op/coreamp.t 4 -- the lvalue-subroutine family ("Can't modify
#             non-lvalue subroutine call in assignment"), which the file's OWN
#             expected-divergence reason named before s468bc removed it.
#         The perl-tests population is UNCHANGED at 5: both rows are companion
#         files, so the sweep's own DROPS bucket does not move.
#   s456ah MESSAGE TEXT ONLY, no row and no count touched (task #737).  s440
#         swapped Data::Dump for the core Data::Dumper in Pl::PExpr::_dd, which
#         changed the SHAPE of the compiler's drop message, so every message
#         below had gone stale tree-wide (truncated at the first `[`, and no
#         longer what the compiler prints).  Refreshed once from a full
#         `tools/drop-census.pl . OUT 8 --board` on 49e55ad + this session's
#         cl/-only fixes, which reports the same 21 files / 65 drops the rows
#         below carry.  The refresh ASSERTS the file SET and every per-file
#         COUNT byte-identical before it will write, and refuses otherwise: a
#         count that moves during a text refresh is a finding, not a refresh.
#         The rows keep their blessed ORDER, so the diff is message text alone.
#   s456ag SIX rows REMOVED and ONE reduced, TWELVE drops (27/77 -> 21/65).
#         Five mechanisms, each probed against perl 5.40.3 and each carrying
#         its own guard rows; the cpan-`t` population is now at ZERO:
#         (1) A WORD AFTER `->` IS A METHOD NAME (#481 + #482, one predicate
#         Pl::PExpr::_word_is_method_name).  Two passes read such a word as
#         something else and each LOST the statement: extract_declarations
#         stripped `state`/`my`/`our`/`local` as a DECLARATOR (so `$one->state`
#         reached the postfix handler with nothing after the arrow and the
#         compiler died inside PPI's API), and the fat-comma pass AUTOQUOTED it
#         (so `is $csv->module => 'M'` left the arrow with no word).  Removes
#         Test2/API/InterceptResult/Event.pm (1) and one of
#         t/Test2/modules/API/InterceptResult.t's two, and both of
#         Text-CSV-2.04/t/01_is_pp.t.
#         (2) A `(&…)`-PROTOTYPE BLOCK CALL ENDS AT `->`: the slurpy @ consumes
#         juxtaposed TERMS and `->` is not one — it is a postfix operator
#         binding to the call's RESULT, so `intercept {…}->upgrade` is
#         `intercept(sub{…})->upgrade` (probed for `(&)` and `(&;@)`, for a
#         method, `->[0]` and `->{k}`).  Swallowing the arrow left it at the
#         head of an argument list with nothing before it.  Removes
#         t/Legacy/Regression/637.t (1) and InterceptResult.t's other one.
#         (3) PPI §28, `$x.2` (#480): the `.` is absorbed into a Number::Float
#         and there is no operator token at all.  Pl::Parser2::_repair_dot_number,
#         the `_ends_term` family's fourth member.  Removes
#         Text-CSV-2.04/t/78_fragment.t (1).
#         (4) PPI §19b, a bare `x` STARTING a statement: `x` is INFIX, so a
#         statement cannot begin with it, yet PPI does after a sub definition's
#         closing brace — which is how a sub named `x` is called with neither
#         parens nor arguments.  _repair_word_x_call's second arm; the
#         discriminator is PPI's own tree (first significant child of the
#         Statement), which is what leaves `do { … } x 3` alone.  t/op/lexsub.t
#         4 -> 1 (its lines 448, 751 and 836; the remaining drop is the
#         `y, 43, '…'` transliterate shape).
#         (5) ONE readline-name predicate pair (_readline_bareword_name_p /
#         _readline_scalar_name_p): PPI splits `<Ạ>` into `< Ạ >` in most term
#         positions (§14) and _fix_ppi_glob_after_block rebuilds it, but ITS
#         name test was ASCII-only while the readline/glob decision in `parse`
#         had already been made Unicode-aware — so `$a .= <Ạ>` was dropped
#         whole while `my $x = <Ạ>` compiled.  Removes t/uni/readline.t (2).
#         NOTE on that last one: the two rows behind it will now RUN and FAIL
#         honestly, because the paren-LESS `open Ạ, …` still puts the name
#         through the ALL-CAPS `[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*` bareword-handle heuristic
#         (task #820, PRE-EXISTING and separate).  That is the s438h pattern —
#         a fix that makes values real exposes what was passing on nothing.
#         The MESSAGE TEXT of the rows this session did not touch is older than
#         the rows themselves: `Pl::PExpr::_dd` became one-line at s440d, so a
#         fresh run prints the full token dump where a row blessed before that
#         kept only the text up to the first newline.  Counts are unaffected —
#         they are what the runners compare — and the text is left alone rather
#         than re-blessed, per the row-by-row rule.
#   s454ae SEVEN rows REMOVED and ONE reduced, THIRTEEN drops (34/90 -> 27/77),
#         by two mechanisms, both verified by re-running the harvest over the
#         cpan+board rows after each change (gate NOT yet run -- stop-order
#         session; the merging session must run the full bar):
#         (1) CODE ASSIGNED TO A TYPEGLOB IS A SUB DECLARATION, prototype
#         included: `BEGIN { *try = \&_manual_try }` (Test2::Util's shape)
#         now registers `try (&;@)` -- Pl::Parser::glob_sub_alias_fact /
#         glob_sub_alias_stmts / _glob_alias_sig_info, consumed by the module
#         facts walk (collect_prototypes: every load-time assignment) and by
#         Parser2's pre-scan (BEGIN blocks only -- within the same file only a
#         BEGIN-time assignment is a compile-time fact).  Clears Context.pm 1,
#         Instance.pm 2, IPC/Driver/Files.pm 1, Tools/Tiny.pm 1,
#         IPC/Driver/Files.t 1; with the ceiling half below, Util.pm 1
#         (`HAVE_PERLIO ? grep {...} ... : ()` -- the BEGIN-aliased
#         `sub() {1}` makes HAVE_PERLIO a zero-arg term).  Probes p2/p3/p4
#         vs perl in the session log.
#         (1b) THE BLOCK-FORM ARGUMENT RUN GETS THE SAME CEILING as every
#         other paren-less list operator: _take_rest_as_args used to consume
#         to END OF STREAM, so `$c ? grep { ... } @a : ()` swallowed the
#         `: ()` (orphaned colon, statement dropped) and `grep { ... } @a
#         or EXPR` swallowed the `or` (a SILENT WRONG, probed:
#         `my $r = grep { $_ > 1 } (1,2,3) or print` gave r=1 where perl
#         says r=2).  ONE shared helper _listop_arg_ceiling (and/or/xor +
#         enclosing-ternary ':') now serves the operator-loop path AND
#         _take_rest_as_args (rule 11).
#         (2) A module's subs are in its STASH whatever the import list says:
#         _merge_module_prototypes registers the module env's prototype facts
#         under the MODULE's package (Environment::add_pkg_prototype,
#         per-package table ONLY -- flat/unqualified resolution unchanged),
#         and _proto_entry answers a QUALIFIED spelling from the per-package
#         table first.  Clears API.t 4 (`Test2::API::context_do { ... }`,
#         `Test2::API::no_context { ... }` -- context_do was never imported)
#         and Mojo _Collection.pm 4 -> 2 (`List::Util::first { ... } @$self`;
#         the module also declares its OWN `first`, which is why the flat
#         table could never answer).  The 2 that stay are the
#         `local (*{"${caller}::a"}, ...)` family -- a LOUD Parser2 TODO
#         (#564's neighborhood), message refreshed in the row.
#   s448o -1 drop (task #562, the residue s446k left): t/re/pat.t 3 -> 2, so
#         the file total goes 34 rows / 89 drops -> 34 / 88 (the row stays, it
#         keeps two).  `*^R = *caretRglobwithnoscalar;` (pat.t:1715) is not the
#         glob named `^` -- perl's caret convention means the glob named
#         chr(18), the one `$^R` reads -- so `*{'^'}R` would have been a silent
#         wrong and s446k left it dropping on purpose.  The repair now spells
#         the CONTROL CHARACTER (`*{'<chr18>'}`), which is what perl means, and
#         the runtime's %p-slot-name maps a one-control-character glob name
#         onto PCL's `$^R` spelling, so the alias actually takes instead of
#         writing a symbol nothing reads.  Measured: the arms disabled give
#         pat.t 3 and enabled give 2; emission A/B over perl's t/ + cpan-tests
#         (988 files) has pat.t as the ONLY DIFF, RCDIFF 0; corpus-diff
#         IDENTICAL over 111 with silent drops 5 unchanged; lib A/B 29/29 SAME.
#         The task's OTHER shape, `*]` (t/op/tie_fetch_count.t:189), is fixed
#         in the same walk but changes NO row here: that file is refused whole
#         at line 169 (`~~`), so it emits nothing and has never had a census
#         row.  Guard Pl/t/punct-glob-name-01.t 8 -> 12 rows.
#   s441b -1 file / -4 drops (task #463 item 1): `$${EXPR}`.  PPI lexes the
#         `$$` as the PID Magic and the braces as a SUBSCRIPT (they follow a
#         variable token); perl reads `${ ${EXPR} }`.  The Magic->two-casts
#         pre-pass has been there since #305, but it left the braces a
#         Subscript, and Cast+Cast+Subscript is a hash-element access with NO
#         base -- the cast-consuming loop declined and dropped the statement.
#         The pre-pass now also re-classes those braces to the Block that
#         `${EXPR}` arrives as.  t/uni/gv.t 2 -> 0 (row leaves), t/op/gv.t
#         3 -> 1 (its remaining drop is the unrelated "Missing case: [").
#         Measured: emission A/B over all 528 companion files DIFF = exactly
#         these two; corpus-diff IDENTICAL over 111 + 6 shapes; lib A/B
#         SAME=21; the shape occurs in NO other file in any population.  The
#         two files' ROWS do not move (134/65 and 55/33) -- both abort earlier
#         for unrelated reasons -- so only their drops columns are edited.
#   s441a -2 files / -3 drops (task #463 item 2): prefix `++`/`--` on a
#         SCALAR DEREF parses now, so `t/op/universal.t` (1) and
#         `t/uni/method.t` (2) leave.  `op_info` calls every PPI Cast a
#         one-operand prefix operator of precedence 90 and `++`/`--` are the
#         only prefix operators ABOVE that (92), so the operator loop reduced
#         the increment FIRST and handed it the bare `$` cast token as its
#         whole operand -- `parse([Cast])` has no case for a lone cast, the
#         term walker declined, and the statement went.  One predicate
#         (`_is_prefix_op_token`) now answers YES for a Cast, which routes the
#         pair through the loop's existing "adjacent prefix operators reduce
#         INNER-first" walk.  Measured: emission A/B over all 528 companion
#         files shows exactly these two DIFF, corpus-diff IDENTICAL over 111,
#         lib A/B SAME=21, and a text scan of all six populations finds the
#         shape in no other file.  Rows: t/op/universal.t C_ok 61 -> 79.
#   s441b NINE drops REMOVED and FOUR FILES CLEARED, by task #464: a trailing
#         STATEMENT MODIFIER on a statement class whose lowering slices the
#         statement's tokens by position.  ONE cause: the modifier split lived
#         inside _process_expression_statement, so `require` + everything after
#         it, and `local(LHS) =` + everything after the `=`, handed the
#         modifier straight to the expression parser -- which then had a bare
#         `if` Word with no operator around it and answered "Bug. Fell through.
#         Missing case: [".  Two shared halves now, one copy each in
#         Pl/Parser.pm: _split_trailing_modifier (take it off, with the set of
#         words THIS caller can lower) + _wrap_statement_modifier (wrap the
#         lowered form).  `require` accepts all six modifiers -- it is an
#         ordinary runtime op, so p-if/p-unless/p-while/p-until/p-foreach say
#         exactly what perl says; `local` accepts only if/unless, because perl
#         restores a `local ... for (1,2)` at the end of each iteration and
#         PCL's open let cannot express that, so a loop modifier there keeps
#         DROPPING (loudly) rather than becoming a silent wrong.
#           Test2/API/Context.pm            2 -> 1   (line 20, require unless)
#           Test2/API/InterceptResult.pm    1 -> 0
#           Test2/API/InterceptResult/Event.pm 3 -> 1 (lines 90 + 138)
#           Test2/Formatter/TAP.pm          2 -> 0   (lines 111 + 155, local LIST)
#           board Sub/Uplevel.pm            1 -> 0   (line 49, require if)
#         Verified over ALL FOUR populations vs 61ea4b5: corpus-diff IDENTICAL
#         (111 files, drops 5), lib A/B SAME=22, perl-t A/B SAME=528, cpan A/B
#         402 files with exactly those four as the DIFFs (RCDIFF=0 throughout).
#         Guard Pl/t/stmt-modifier-01.t (12 rows; every expectation re-run under
#         real perl, and one row asserts the loop-modifier drop is still loud),
#         inverse-run on the base Pl/Parser.pm = 22 failing rows.  80/183 ->
#         TWO ROWS IN THIS EDIT ARE NOT THIS CHANGE'S, and are named so nobody
#         attributes them to it: board Text/Balanced.pm's 2 drops (#457) were
#         ALREADY ZERO at 7e6d1eb -- measured with the base Pl/Parser.pm in
#         place -- so they left in one of s438b..s438i and were never
#         re-measured because the board population is opt-in; and
#         Text-CSV t/01_is_pp.t's message TEXT changed with s440's Data::Dump
#         -> Data::Dumper switch in the diagnostics (its count is unmoved at 2).
#   s441b TWO drops REMOVED, ONE FILE CLEARED, by task #466: a MAGIC scalar in
#         the FILEHANDLE slot of print/printf/say.  perl's grammar is
#         `listop: LSTOP indirob listexpr` with `indirob: WORD | scalar |
#         block`, and `scalar` is ANY scalar variable -- so `print $_ "x\n"`
#         is a write to the handle $_ holds, exactly like `print $fh "x\n"`.
#         PPI hands the punctuation/digit/caret spellings over as
#         PPI::Token::Magic, a SUBCLASS of PPI::Token::Symbol, and all three
#         of PCL's filehandle-slot tests were exact-class `ref($t) eq
#         'PPI::Token::Symbol'`: they answered "not a scalar", no filehandle
#         was extracted, and the leftover `$_ "x\n"` run had two terms with no
#         operator between them -- the whole statement fell through.  ONE
#         predicate now answers for all three sites (Pl::PExpr::
#         _is_scalar_fh_token: the operator-loop print path, the
#         `print $fh -e $f` filetest repair, the paren form `print($fh ...)`).
#         Verified over ALL FOUR populations vs 7e6d1eb: corpus-diff IDENTICAL
#         (111 files, drops 5), lib A/B SAME=22, perl-t A/B SAME=528, cpan A/B
#         402 files with NoOutput.pm the ONLY DIFF (RCDIFF=0 either way).
#         Guard Pl/t/print-fh-magic-01.t (11 rows, 4 of them negatives),
#         inverse-run with the old exact-class test = 14 failures.  81/185 ->
#   s438  +42 files / +83 drops, the whole `cpan-t` population arriving at
#         once (task #473, ruled s437).  NOT a regression and not new: these
#         sites have been dropping since before the flip -- an f702da3
#         worktree gives the identical 42 files / 83 drops -- they were simply
#         in no population.  Where they came from:
#           79 of 83 are ONE mechanism, task #478: the prototype pre-scan
#              SKIPS every Test2::/Test:: module BY NAME, so a block-form call
#              to a dist-declared `(&)` sub (intercept 53, exception 8,
#              capture 7, warnings 4, no_context 3, context_do 2, Text::CSV's
#              try/async 2) is not a block-form call.  The discriminating
#              probe is two identical modules differing only in the package
#              NAME.  The no-semicolon spelling of the same call does not drop
#              -- it mis-parses SILENTLY -- which is why this row group is
#              worth more than its count.
